recommendations.headline: Only 18% of calls convert to orders, but when customers are satisfied the win rate jumps to 71% (vs 10% neutral, 2% dissatisfied) - satisfaction and follow-through, not price, are the real conversion levers.
behaviour: 55% of calls (1,591/2,879) end in a callback rather than a decision, showing long consideration cycles.
Price is not even discussed in 68% of calls (1,966/2,879), yet price_shopper (575) and comparing_quotes (335) are top behaviour tags - customers are benchmarking before engaging on price.
Stock availability (524 mentions) and fast delivery (486) are the top stated needs, ahead of price negotiation itself.
Repeat (265) and bulk (318) buyers form a large, recurring demand base alongside 286 urgent buyers who need speed, not just price.
Competitor_cheaper objections (119) convert worst of all objection types at just 8% win rate, showing price comparison conversations are currently being lost.
satisfaction: Satisfaction is the single strongest predictor of sales success: satisfied calls win 71% of the time vs 10% for neutral and 2% for dissatisfied calls.
Only 30% of calls (851/2,879) are rated satisfied; 55% are neutral and 10% dissatisfied - most calls leave customers uncommitted.
Price_high is raised in 489 calls (17%) but still wins 22% of the time - objections like stock_availability (16% win) and credit_terms (13% win) hurt conversion more than price itself.
Price reactions show only 8% outright acceptance (239) and 4% 'too high' (109) - the real blocker is calls stalling before price is even reached (68% not_discussed).

conversion.title: Fix the follow-up gap
conversion.evidence: no_follow_up_fixed is the top rep miss at 536 calls (19%), while 55% of all calls end in callback.
conversion.action: Require every rep to set a specific date/time for the next contact before ending the call and log it in CRM; managers audit weekly.

conversion.title: Speed up and clarify answers
conversion.evidence: slow_or_unclear_answer flagged in 486 calls (17%).
conversion.action: Give reps a live stock/price reference sheet and scripted quick-answers for common size/grade/stock questions.

conversion.title: Send quotes faster and always
conversion.evidence: no_quote_sent in 304 calls (11%); no_quote_sent + no_follow_up together explain much of the 55% stuck-in-callback pipeline.
conversion.action: Mandate a written quote (WhatsApp/email) within a fixed time window on every price enquiry, tracked for compliance.

conversion.title: Always ask for the order
conversion.evidence: didnt_ask_for_order flagged in 205 calls (7%) despite many customers being ready (515 orders, 270 interested).
conversion.action: Train reps to explicitly ask for confirmation/PO once price and stock are agreed, rather than leaving it open-ended.

conversion.title: Offer alternatives on stock-outs
conversion.evidence: stock_availability is the #2 objection (459 calls, only 16% win) and didnt_offer_alternative flagged 215 times.
conversion.action: Give reps real-time visibility of stock across all branches and train them to always propose a substitute size/grade/location when the exact item is unavailable.

conversion.title: Win back competitor-comparison calls
conversion.evidence: competitor_cheaper has the lowest win rate of all objections at 8% (119 calls), vs JSW (43), SAIL (20), Jindal (18) most-cited competitors.
conversion.action: Equip reps with a value script (certification, consistency, cutting service) to use instead of price-matching when competitors are named.

conversion.title: Prioritise and qualify the 'unknown' segment
conversion.evidence: Unknown segment is the 2nd largest (716 calls) but converts worst at 15% win, vs dealer 31% and fabricator 37%.
conversion.action: Train reps to ask business type/segment early in the call to tailor the pitch and route follow-up correctly.

offers.for_whom: Fabricators and project buyers needing custom sizes
offers.why: cutting_processing is the 4th highest need (284 mentions) and repeatedly asked about in calls (cutting charge, tolerance, wastage).

offers.title: Multi-branch stock check and reservation
offers.why: stock_availability is both the top need (524) and the #2 objection (459, 16% win).

offers.why: quality_doubt objection (206) and test_certificate need (190) recur, plus multiple calls about mismatched/missing certificates.

offers.why: regular_updates is a top need (370) and customers explicitly ask for a 'rate card like other companies'.

offers.for_whom: Repeat and bulk buyers with consistent order history
offers.why: credit_terms objection (128, only 13% win) and needs_credit behaviour (148) indicate unmet demand.

loyalty.how: Flag repeat_buyer/bulk_buyer accounts in CRM for faster quote turnaround and a dedicated contact person.
loyalty.why: 265 repeat_buyer and 318 bulk_buyer tags show a sizable loyal base worth formal recognition.

loyalty.why: no_follow_up_fixed (536 misses) is the top rep gap; reliability builds trust without discounting.

loyalty.title: Referral recognition program
loyalty.how: Acknowledge and thank customers who refer new business, perhaps with priority handling.
loyalty.why: Only 18 referral-tagged calls currently - an untapped loyalty lever.

loyalty.title: Self-serve order/certificate access
loyalty.how: Consider a WhatsApp group or simple portal for repeat/industrial clients to retrieve past orders and test certificates.
loyalty.why: Multiple calls raise repeat questions about certificates, batch numbers and past deliveries, adding friction.

non_price_benefits.why: consistent_supply (231) and stock_availability (524) are top-cited needs across calls.

non_price_benefits.why: quality_doubt (206 objections) and test_certificate (190 needs) are recurring concerns, including cast-number mismatches.

non_price_benefits.why: needs_technical_help (372 behaviour) and technical_advice (215 need) show customers value guidance on grade/size selection.

top_questions.question: What is the current rate for this item?
top_questions.answer_tip: State the rate's validity window clearly, flag any upcoming change, and follow up immediately with a written quote.

top_questions.question: Is this size/grade in stock, and where?
top_questions.answer_tip: Check real-time stock across all branches before answering; if unavailable, offer the closest alternative size, grade, or branch.

top_questions.question: Can you send the proforma invoice/PO quickly?
top_questions.answer_tip: Clarify your standard sequence (PO then proforma or vice versa) upfront so there's no back-and-forth delay.

top_questions.question: Will a test certificate (MTC) be provided, and does it match the material?
top_questions.answer_tip: Confirm certificate provision proactively and ensure batch/cast numbers are checked before dispatch to avoid disputes.

top_questions.question: Can you reduce the price / match a competitor's rate?
top_questions.answer_tip: Acknowledge the comparison, then highlight certification, stock reliability, and service quality instead of matching price; escalate only per policy.

top_questions.question: When exactly will the material be delivered/loaded?
top_questions.answer_tip: Give a specific committed date/time and proactively flag any holiday or logistics delay in advance.

top_questions.question: Why is the transport/loading charge so high?
top_questions.answer_tip: Break down transport and loading costs transparently at quotation stage, not after order confirmation.

top_questions.question: Do you offer credit terms?
top_questions.answer_tip: Explain current credit policy and eligibility criteria clearly; flag strong repeat accounts for management review of credit terms.

recommendations.headline: Varsha's calls mostly end as open callbacks (1,347 of 2,426 = 55.5%) with no fixed next step (459 calls flagged no_follow_up_fixed) and stay 'neutral' in satisfaction (56.6%) - neutral calls convert at only 10% vs 72% for satisfied ones, so tightening follow-up discipline and answer clarity is the single biggest lever to move the 18% order rate.
behaviour: Price shopping dominates: 449 calls tagged price_shopper and 262 comparing_quotes, with named competitors (JSW 29, SAIL/NMDC/Jindal 14 each) coming up on calls.
Customers stall rather than refuse: 55.5% of calls end in callback vs only 18.2% in order and 4.5% not_interested - most leads are kept warm but not closed.
Top unmet needs are logistics, not just price: stock_availability (439), fast_delivery (423) and regular_updates (312) outrank pure price asks in the needs list.
Objections cluster almost equally on price_high (400) and stock_availability (395), ahead of quality_doubt (185) and delivery_time (166).

Dealers are the biggest segment (1,226 calls) but convert at only 31%, and 626 calls (26%) have no segment identified at all with the lowest win rate (15%) - Varsha is not always qualifying who she's talking to.
satisfaction: Only 28.6% of calls are rated satisfied; 56.6% are neutral and 10.5% dissatisfied - the bulk of calls leave the customer non-committal.
Satisfaction is the strongest predictor of winning a sale: satisfied calls convert at 72%, neutral at only 10%, dissatisfied at 3% - far bigger swing than any single objection.

Price is discussed in only 30.5% of calls (not_discussed 1,685 of 2,426); among those discussed, negotiating (459) and accepted (190) far outnumber too_high (92) - price is more often negotiable than a hard blocker (price_blocker_pct is just 20%).

Despite price_high being the top objection (400 calls), its win rate (21%) is actually better than stock_availability (17%), delivery_time (14%) or credit_terms (11%) objections - stock and service issues may be hurting Varsha more than price.

conversion.title: Always fix a concrete next step before ending the call
conversion.evidence: no_follow_up_fixed flagged in 459 calls (18.9%) and callback is the outcome in 55.5% of all calls
conversion.action: End every call with a specific date/time for the next contact or delivery, and log it immediately so it's never left open-ended.

conversion.title: Give faster, clearer answers on stock, rate and timelines
conversion.evidence: slow_or_unclear_answer flagged in 424 calls (17.5%)
conversion.action: Keep an updated stock/rate sheet on hand during calls; if unsure, commit to a specific callback time (e.g. 'within 2 hours') rather than an open 'I'll check'.

conversion.title: Send a written quote on every price enquiry
conversion.evidence: no_quote_sent flagged in 269 calls; price_enquiry is the top intent (741 calls, 30.5% of all calls)
conversion.action: Follow every price discussion with a WhatsApp/email quote same day, even if verbal rate was given.

conversion.title: Offer an alternative immediately when stock/size is unavailable
conversion.evidence: didnt_offer_alternative flagged in 189 calls; stock_availability is the #2 objection (395 calls, win 17%)
conversion.action: When the exact size/grade isn't in stock, proactively suggest nearest available size, other branch stock, or cutting to size instead of just promising to check.

conversion.title: Explicitly ask for the order when the customer is ready
conversion.evidence: didnt_ask_for_order flagged in 155 calls; several 'well' summaries show customers confirming price/specs but call ends without a clear ask
conversion.action: Once price, grade and quantity are confirmed, directly ask for PO/payment instead of waiting for the customer to initiate.

conversion.title: Lead with value before discounting
conversion.evidence: didnt_highlight_value flagged in 92 calls; satisfied calls win at 72% vs 10% for neutral, showing value perception matters more than price itself
conversion.action: Mention certification, cutting service, delivery reliability and stock depth before any rate negotiation starts.

conversion.title: Confirm full requirement upfront to avoid rework
conversion.evidence: didnt_ask_requirement flagged in 58 calls; quality_doubt (185) and multiple questions about grade/cast-number mismatches recur in summaries
conversion.action: Always confirm grade, size, quantity and cutting length at the start of the call and repeat it back before quoting.

recommendations.headline: Venkatesh is losing deals on his own execution, not on price: 244 of 453 calls (54%) end as a vague 'callback' with no fixed follow-up logged 77 times, and he fails to ask for the order in 50 calls — fixing these two habits matters more than discounting.
behaviour: 126 of 453 customers are price shoppers and 73 are actively comparing quotes, so most calls need a clear, fast quote, not just conversation.
64 are bulk buyers and 38 are repeat buyers, showing a core of high-value relationships worth protecting with service, not price cuts.
Customers most want stock_availability info (85), fast_delivery (63) and regular_updates (58) — these outrank credit_period (25) and technical_advice (23) as reasons they call.

Objection win-rates show price_high actually converts at 30%, while stock_availability (11% win) and competitor_cheaper (9% win) convert far worse — the real deal-killers are availability and positioning, not rate.
High urgency calls are only 52 of 453 (11%), so most buyers (278 medium, 103 low) can be nurtured with good follow-up rather than rushed.
satisfaction: Satisfied calls convert at 65% vs only 10% for neutral calls (221 of them) — Venkatesh's call handling, not price, is the biggest swing factor in closing.
62% of calls (281/453) never reach a clear price discussion (price_reaction 'not_discussed') — many prospects are leaving without even hearing a number.
Only 27 calls (6%) are flagged dissatisfied but they convert at 0%, confirming poor-experience calls are a dead loss regardless of price.
Price_high objection still wins 30% of the time it's raised, showing most customers accept the price once engaged — the issue is follow-through, not affordability.
